ACCEPTThe final additions are mathematically sound. In particular, the common resource drop and allocation along original injection links are valid, the closed two-row argument proves the obstruction for every horizontal cancellation matching, and the selected-cap construction correctly compensates the cropped family using empty cancellation and the left caps. The  $H=4$  right-boundary collision is real and is now accounted for correctly.I found no substantive mathematical error requiring a change to the results. Two small clarifications would make the statements especially precise: call the constructed owner allocation maximum-cardinality, and explicitly retain  $u_{\mathrm{cap}}=0$  in the sentence about allocating only  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2$  demands. Both are already supported by the surrounding proof.This review concerns the written mathematics and the scope of the supplied Lean statements. I do not certify any reported execution or checker count.1. The common drop  $R=\sum_K\min(d_K,b_K)$  is exactFor each terminal-graph component  $K$ , let  $d_K,b_K$  count its original alpha and beta owners. The component conservation argument gives:
$$d_K-b_K=
\begin{cases}
1,&K\text{ is a virtual alpha path},\\
0,&K\text{ is a virtual mixed path or a cycle},\\
-1,&K\text{ is a virtual beta path}.
\end{cases}$$
Consequently,
$$d_K-\min(d_K,b_K)=\max(d_K-b_K,0)$$
is exactly the indicator that  $K$  is a virtual alpha, and
$$b_K-\min(d_K,b_K)=\max(b_K-d_K,0)$$
is exactly the indicator that  $K$  is a virtual beta. Summing over components proves
$$\alpha'=\alpha-R,\qquad
\beta'=\beta-R,
\qquad
R=\sum_K\min(d_K,b_K).$$
Since each original owner belongs to exactly one component,
$$0\le R\le \min(\alpha,\beta).$$
This is valid for arbitrary permitted opposite-label cancellation matchings; the original-alpha source restriction is not needed for this numerical identity.The delicate cases remain correct:A mixed-owner two-edge cancellation cycle has  $d_K=b_K=0$ , so contributes nothing to  $R$ .An alpha–beta cycle with two parallel links has  $d_K=b_K=1$ , so consumes exactly one alpha and one beta.A beta owner linked at both terminals still belongs to one component and contributes only one to its  $b_K$ .An alpha–beta–alpha chain has  $d_K=2,b_K=1$ , hence  $R_K=1$  and one residual alpha.Therefore, when  $\beta=0$ ,
$$R=0,\qquad \alpha'=\alpha,\qquad \beta'=0$$
for every permitted cancellation matching, including nonhorizontal ones. The horizontal geometry is needed later to prove that the surviving alpha remains unported; it is not needed to prove persistence of the alpha count.2. Allocation along original injection links is valid under the source restrictionThe additional hypothesis that every TP source belongs to an original alpha owner does real work.After contracting each original strand to its owner, every cancellation edge has one of the forms
$$\text{alpha--beta}
\quad\text{or}\quad
\text{alpha--mixed}.$$
There are no mixed–beta or mixed–mixed links under this hypothesis. Each owner has degree at most two, and a mixed owner has degree at most one because only its single BP terminal can participate.Thus mixed owners are leaves or isolated vertices. Removing them:Does not change the counts  $d_K,b_K$ ;Does not disconnect the remaining alpha–beta core;Leaves an alternating alpha–beta path, cycle, singleton, or an empty core when the original component was an isolated mixed owner.The possible two-parallel-edge alpha–beta cycle is included.An alternating path admits an owner matching of size  $\min(d_K,b_K)$ : take successive alternate edges from an appropriate end. An alternating cycle has equal part sizes and admits a perfect matching by taking alternate edges. Singleton and empty cores contribute zero.Every selected edge remains an actual original cancellation link. Hence this constructs an allocation of
$$R=\sum_K\min(d_K,b_K)$$
distinct original alpha demands to  $R$  distinct original beta resources, with no beta owner reused.Moreover, no matching within component  $K$  can have more than  $\min(d_K,b_K)$  pairs. The construction therefore has maximum cardinality among allocations along those links.The text’s word “maximal” is not false, but “maximum-cardinality” is sharper. An arbitrary maximal matching would not suffice: on an alpha–beta–alpha–beta path, the middle edge alone is maximal but has size one rather than two. Your proof avoids this issue by prescribing the alternating matching.The restriction cannot simply be removedWithout the original-alpha source restriction, one can have an owner chain
$$\text{alpha--mixed--beta},$$
using the mixed BP terminal for the first link and the mixed TP terminal for the second. Its numerical drop is still  $R_K=1$ , but there is no original link directly joining the alpha owner to the beta owner.Thus the note correctly distinguishes:The common-drop identity, valid for arbitrary permitted  $C$ ;Allocation directly along original links, proved under the source restriction.The unallocated original-alpha count is exactly  $\alpha-R=\alpha'$ . This is an exact partial allocation, not a claim that all demands have been paid.3. The closed two-row proof establishes the full horizontal obstructionThe new proof using  $V_*$  is sufficient to justify the universal quantifier over horizontal cancellation matchings.The terminal vertices in rows  $5$  and  $W+4$  have inventory
$$\alpha_*=1,\qquad
\beta_*=0,\qquad
\gamma_*=\frac H2+2.$$
Every original strand meeting  $V_*$  stays inside it:The original alpha joins the two rows.The two upper mixed owners stay in row  $5$ .The  $H/2$  lower mixed owners stay in row  $W+4$ .Every allowed horizontal terminal link from  $V_*$  also stays inside it. The displayed runs contain all terminals in these rows, and the caps are selections rather than terminal vertices. In particular, horizontal links elsewhere in the packet cannot bring an outside ported TP terminal into this closed set.The component containing the original alpha has  $d=1,b=0$ . Its charge is therefore  $-1$ , so it cannot be a cycle and must be a virtual alpha. Every other component has  $d=b=0$ , so it cannot create an additional alpha or beta.The assertion that the residual alpha has one endpoint in each row is also justified. Its original alpha strand is the only edge of either kind connecting the two rows. Since the component is a path containing that edge, deleting that edge separates the path into an upper-row portion and a lower-row portion. Its two free endpoints lie on opposite sides of this separation.Every TP terminal in either row lacks an immediately adjacent BB column. Therefore
$$\alpha'=1,\qquad \beta'=0,\qquad u'=1$$
for every horizontal  $C$ , independently of reassignment, maximality, chronology, or the presence of cancellation cycles.Here  $u'$  is the omitted-strand count for direct BB ports. The later conclusion  $u_{\mathrm{cap}}=0$  for empty cancellation and selected-cap access does not contradict it: the two access relations are different.This is stronger than the earlier Hall argument, and the note now supplies the additional proof needed for that stronger claim.4. The cropped packet has the stated closure and exact positive marginFor
$$J_*=\{4,\ldots,W+5\}\times\{0,\ldots,H+5\},$$
the dimensions are  $W+2$  and  $H+6$ , both even. All selected vertices and matching endpoints remain inside the crop.In fact, the endpoint coordinates satisfy the stronger enclosure
$$P\subseteq
\{5,\ldots,W+4\}\times\{3,\ldots,H+3\}.$$
Thus every axis-aligned  $2\times2$  receiver square containing an original endpoint lies inside
$$\{4,\ldots,W+5\}\times\{2,\ldots,H+4\}
\subseteq J_*.$$
This directly verifies closure for the original endpoint-containing receiver tiles, without requiring an assumption about which corner of such a tile contains the endpoint. Also, under the fixed physical  $2\times2$  tile convention, the crop begins at even coordinates and ends at odd coordinates in both directions, so it is a union of whole physical tiles.I would add this coordinate enclosure to the proof of the receiver-closure sentence. It makes the ownership claim explicit and avoids relying merely on the fact that all occupied vertices were retained.The crop removes no occupied vertex or freezing witness. Consequently feasibility, the actual matching, the terminal graph, and the relevant freezing dependencies remain unchanged.Both extreme columns,  $0$  and  $H+5$ , are BB in every band. There are  $(W+2)/2$  bands, all sealed, so
$$B_*=W+2.$$
The unchanged occupied inventories give
$$\begin{aligned}
S_*
&=\frac{(W+2)(H+6)}2-(H+9)-(W+H)\\
&=\frac{WH}{2}+2W-H-3.
\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$S_*-B_*
=\left(\frac W2-1\right)H+W-5.$$
For the allowed parameters,
$$\left(\frac W2-1\right)H+W-5\ge 2\cdot4+1=9.$$
The smallest case therefore has exactly
$$S_*=17,\qquad B_*=8,\qquad L_*=S_*+1=18.$$
With no direct connector, its ten unmarked interval vertices and one omitted alpha give
$$h'_0-u'=10-1=9=S_*-B_*.$$
The crop substantially reduces the reserve but preserves a strict positive margin. It remains a rule obstruction, not an inequality counterexample.5. The selected-cap adapter has the required ownership propertiesThe enlarged access relation is sufficiently precise:The three columns are consecutive and lie in the same band;All three lie inside  $J$ ;Reflection is permitted;The BT mediator’s selection lies in the same physical row as the terminal endpoint.The last condition specifies the geometry independently of whether that row is the upper or lower row of the band. Thus the construction handles virtual terminals with either orientation. “BT” here is the unordered column type consisting of one blank and one selected corner.No vertical-mate assumption is required. The argument refers only to the free terminal’s original physical position and to the unchanged column types.Interval-side capacityFix one side of one physical BB–TT interval and inspect the immediately external column.If it is TP, the only possible access on that side is direct access from its unique terminal.If it is BT, a selected-cap user must be in the next column, which must be TP. The mediator’s selected row fixes the required endpoint row, and that TP column contains only one terminal.These cases are mutually exclusive.Any other immediately external type supplies neither kind of access.An accessed BB column is an interval end because the immediately preceding TP or BT column does not belong to the BB–TT interval.Consequently, a fixed side has at most one candidate terminal user. After selecting one access per used free terminal, an interval has degree at most two, with a loop consuming both incidences.Mediator capacityThe additional mediator argument is also correct. A particular BT mediator can support a selected-cap access only if one neighboring column is TP and the other BB. These types determine its orientation and its sole candidate terminal.It cannot simultaneously support another selected-cap user from the other side, because that would require the same neighboring columns to exchange the incompatible TP and BB types. The mediator is not itself an endpoint, and it contributes no additional credit.Boundary marksA marked interval touching a packet boundary still has no access on its outward side. A cap access cannot evade that restriction, because all three columns must lie inside  $J$ .Thus marked interval degree remains at most one, and no marked interval can lie on a connector cycle. The original distinctness of boundary marks is unchanged.The Euler calculation therefore gives exactly
$$S-B=h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0+\beta'
-h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2-u_{\mathrm{cap}}.$$
This is a valid general adapter theorem for arbitrary permitted terminal matching  $C$  and arbitrary permitted selected subsets of extended connectors.Scope of the sufficient conditionWith full extended coverage,  $u_{\mathrm{cap}}=0$ , so
$$S-B=h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0+\beta'-h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2.$$
Therefore either  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2=0$ , or an allocation of its demands to distinct  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0/\beta'$  resources, suffices.For clarity, I recommend making the inherited coverage condition explicit in the “more generally” sentence:If  $u_{\mathrm{cap}}=0$ , an allocation of the  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2$  demands to distinct unmarked connector-path or virtual-beta resources suffices.For partial coverage, the demand count is instead
$$h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2+u_{\mathrm{cap}}.$$
The surrounding proof and equation (7) already support this reading.6. Empty cancellation and the left caps compensate the cropped familyThe left-cap application is correct, including the claim that the targets are unmarked.For  $C=\varnothing$ , the alpha terminals remain at column  $3$ . In their respective bands they use the reflected patterns
$$\mathrm{TP}_3-\mathrm{BT}_2-\mathrm{BB}_1.$$
The two mediator selections are  $(5,2)$  and  $(W+4,2)$ , each in the same physical row as its terminal.The target at column  $1$  is an isolated interval vertex: its neighboring columns are BB at  $0$  and BT at  $2$ . Crucially, two consecutive BB columns are not joined in the interval graph; an interval edge requires a TT column. Therefore BB column  $1$  is not part of the first-boundary marked interval at column  $0$ .The two targets lie in distinct bands, are unmarked, and are different interval owners. Adding the single alpha connector merges two isolated unmarked vertices into one unmarked path. This changes the relevant inventories by
$$u_{\mathrm{cap}}:1\longmapsto0,
\qquad
h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0:S_*+1-B_*
\longmapsto S_*-B_*.$$
Thus one unit of actual interval reserve pays the one alpha demand, with no additional credit attributed to either cap selection.The argument is uniform in  $W,H$ . Translated separated copies use distinct terminals, mediators, interval sides, and interval vertices, so the same allocation pays every copy’s demand.Cancellation can destroy these useful accessesAfter the first injection, both free endpoints move to column  $5$ . Their immediate neighboring columns are BP at  $4$  and BP at  $6$ . Hence neither direct nor selected-cap access is available there.This is an important and correct conclusion: preservation of signed credit does not imply monotonic preservation of access to interval resources. Choosing  $C=\varnothing$  is an authorized choice in the general theorem and can be better for the compensation construction.The cropped  $H=4$  right-boundary collisionAfter maximal rightward continuation, the targets are:
$$\text{upper target: BB column }9,
\qquad
\text{lower target: BB column }H+5.$$
If  $H=4$ , both targets are at the cropped final column  $9$ . They are distinct marked vertices in distinct bands. Joining them produces one twice-marked path:
$$h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2=1.$$
If  $H>4$ , the upper target at column  $9$  is interior and unmarked, while the lower target remains final-boundary marked. The connector then has one mark, so  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2=0$ .Writing  $E=S_*-B_*$ , the relevant outcomes are:Cancellation and access choice $u_{\mathrm{cap}}$  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2$  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0$ MarginEmpty cancellation; left caps $0$  $0$  $E$  $E$ First injection; no available extended access $1$  $0$  $E+1$  $E$ Maximal continuation; right caps;  $H=4$  $0$  $1$  $E+1$  $E$ Maximal continuation; right caps;  $H>4$  $0$  $0$  $E$  $E$ Here  $\beta'=0$  throughout.At  $W=6,H=4$ , the right-cap choice has  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_0=10$  and  $h^{\mathrm{cap}}_2=1$ , giving the correct margin  $9$ . It fails the zero-collision sufficient condition, but it does not fail the inequality. The final text makes that distinction correctly.7. The uniform freezing and unique-matching schedules are validI rechecked the schedules as all-parameter arguments.The critical distinction is preserved throughout: an endpoint witness is retained when its actual mate froze earlier. The proof does not replace that condition by the witness itself having frozen.Some potentially delicate transitions are valid as follows: $U_3$  is retained from the initial freezing of  $L_3$ . $U_5$  is retained after  $U_6$  freezes, so the event at  $U_4$  has both required witnesses.The forward loop starts at  $B_6$ : its witnesses  $B_5$  and  $A_6$  are retained because  $(5,5)$  and  $A_5$  already froze.After  $B_r$  freezes,  $B_{r+1}$  is retained and can witness the next event at  $A_{r+1}$ .The backward loop starts because  $A_R=L_3$  and  $B_{R-1}=U_4$  have already frozen.The final lower-strip loop starts at  $L_4$ :  $L_3$  is retained from the forward-loop freezing of  $U_3$ , and  $U_4$  is retained from the freezing of  $B_{R-2}$ .Each subsequent lower-strip advance uses the just-frozen actual mate of its next retained witness.The listed events are distinct and cover all  $2(W+H)$  endpoints. The witnesses are adjacent, nonmate, and selected or retained strictly earlier. Cropping removes none of them.For unique matching, the argument correctly takes leaves in the endpoint-induced graph. Selected neighbors are not additional matching candidates. The initial three forced edges, the vertical-column loop, and the final lower-strip loop all have the stated leaf property. Their  $W+H$  disjoint edges exhaust  $P$ , proving uniqueness.These are uniform constructive proofs. Their validity does not depend on the reported serial-event or forced-edge totals.8. The formal scope and the distinction from a universal grid theorem are accurateThe added Lean statements have the stated mathematical scope:Nonnegativity of alpha and beta list inventories;Noncreation of beta under the defined surgery;Existence of a common nonnegative drop bounded by both initial inventories;Persistence of alpha when the initial beta count is zero.The common-drop proof chooses
$$\text{consumed}=\beta_{\mathrm{before}}-\beta_{\mathrm{after}},$$
and combines beta monotonicity, signed conservation, and nonnegative final inventories. That is the correct arithmetic argument.What remains written rather than formalized includes the identification
$$\text{consumed}=\sum_K\min(d_K,b_K)$$
through the terminal-graph component adapter, allocation along actual injection links, the closed two-row geometry, receiver closure, cap ownership, boundary classification, and the uniform grid schedules. The note does not claim otherwise.The final results are correctly separated:The cancellation and extended-connector identities are general bookkeeping theorems under their hypotheses.Allocation along original links requires the original-alpha source restriction.The frozen family defeats every strategy that tries to expose both direct ports using only horizontal cancellation.Selected-cap access provides a proved compensation construction for the entire displayed family and its separated copies.A universal grid inequality still requires general coverage or allocation of the residual demands, including twice-marked paths. The final note expressly leaves that obligation open.
